page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.16-64 is an x86_64 compute instance configured with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates two hardware threads per physical core and provides 64.0 GB of system memory, corresponding to 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local NVMe or solid-state storage is included with the base instance, requiring users to rely on external network-attached block volumes for persistent data storage.

Hardware capabilities do not include hardware acceleration, as the instance features zero graphics processing units. Network provisioning comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the memory allocation maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration aligns with compute-oriented workloads where CPU density takes precedence over large working memory footprints.

Without integrated local disks, input and output performance is directly tied to the performance profile and bandwidth limits of attached remote volumes. This setup offers predictable compute execution suitable for batch processing, continuous integration and build pipelines, compute-bound microservices, and distributed worker nodes that do not require massive in-memory caching or localized high-IOPS disk arrays.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.16-64 is a flexible x86_64 compute instance equipped with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a tight 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio suitable for compute-centric processing. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on remote block storage for persistence. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated hardware thread allocation across its 16 cores, the instance provides steady CPU throughput for environments requiring consistent computational performance, including distributed compile jobs, backend application services, video or batch data processing, and container orchestration nodes.
